sources.locator: "Deportation of the Crimean Tatars", revision 1375533569, § lead

explanation: The English article says the Soviet government presented the deportation as collective punishment, on its claim that some Crimean Tatars collaborated with Nazi Germany in the war — noting that the 20,000 who collaborated with the Axis were half the 40,000 who served in the Red Army — and that several modern scholars instead believe the deportation was part of a plan to gain access to the Dardanelles and acquire territory in Turkey, or to clear minorities from the border regions. The war is the occasion the government gave; the article is explicit that scholars dispute that it is the reason.
